column1: # One row per served image shape. A profile_id names a bundle in
# remote/image-models.tsv at one placement arm and one request geometry, and
# several profiles reach one bundle the way several web profiles reach one
# checkpoint in remote/web-profiles.tsv.
# placement names where each component executes, and the appliance decides
# which arm wins by measurement rather than by reasoning: `A` puts the text
# encoder, the diffusion trunk, and the VAE on Vulkan; `B` runs the text
# encoder on the CPU with diffusion and VAE on Vulkan; `C` runs the text
# encoder and the VAE on the CPU with diffusion alone on Vulkan. The arm binds
# the bundle's own composition, so remote/image-registry.sh requires arm B to
# name a text encoder and arm C to name a text encoder and a VAE -- a bundle
# that omits the component an arm places has no arm to place it on. The LLM
# ladder is the reason the arms exist rather than a single answer: every tested
# hybrid placement lost to full Vulkan there because both sides draw on the one
# DDR4 controller, and whether a diffusion graph repeats that result is
# unmeasured.
# width, height, and steps are what the profile requests; max_dimension and
# max_steps are what it admits. The registry requires width and height at or
# below max_dimension and steps at or below max_steps, so an authorization
# grant that names a larger image is refused against the profile rather than
# against the runtime. timeout_s is the runtime's own hard bound, and the
# service, MCP, router, and browser deadlines stack above it so a stalled run
# is ended by the process that owns it.
# execution_policy decides what the profile may do, over `refused` and
# `validator-gated`, mirroring remote/web-profiles.tsv. `refused` runs nothing:
# the profile is an admitted shape and no generation executes against it.
# `validator-gated` admits a generation behind an authorization grant that
# binds prompt hash, seed, dimensions, and step count, and it requires
# validated_evidence to name a retained record that exists in the tree, because
# a profile that may spend the device must carry the run that showed it safe.
# One row reads `validator-gated`: image-sdxs-512-a carries the served turn of
# evidence/image-appliance/served-turn-admission/, where an approved generation
# reached the runtime through router, broker, MCP child, and service and every
# refusal the design rests on fired once. Every other row reads `refused` and
# admits a shape alone; a measured campaign on the appliance is what moves the
# next one.
# validated_evidence is a repository-relative path, `-` where no run has been
# retained. Any path present must exist in the tree whatever the policy reads,
# so a record removed from the tree refuses the query rather than leaving a
# claim pointing at nothing.
# review_model pairs one vision checkpoint with this image shape, because the
# reviewer belongs to the profile that produced the artifact rather than to the
# conversation that asked for it. `-` offers no review. image-sdxs-512-a names
# lfm25-vl-16b, because the appliance's own budget gate admitted the pair at
# 4388 MiB against 11.42 GiB of Vulkan margin and one page session then ran an
# approved generation and a parsed review of its artifact
# (evidence/image-appliance/paired-review-admission/). Every other row reads
# `-`, since a second resident checkpoint has to fit beside the language row
# inside the Vulkan budget this machine carves and only the appliance holds
# that probe. A named value is a remote/models.tsv model_id
# whose projector column reads `required`; remote/build-web-presets.sh joins it
# against that registry, requires a projector on disk and a validated tuple with
# the projector loaded, and emits a review-only section beside the language one.
# That section carries the vision row's own tuple and its projector, names no
# MCP configuration, and offers no tool, so the page reviews an artifact through
# it and reaches nothing else.
